narrative: Across this week's feeds, fire and climate work stood out: Holocene records from northwestern Quebec show how topography shaped fire regimes and vegetation, a Methods in Ecology and Evolution paper introduces sensors to measure wildlife smoke exposure, and Global Change Biology reports intensifying drought risks for rainfed maize, soybean and wheat as warming decouples climate and root-zone drought. In movement and connectivity, new trajectory and step-selection approaches predict connectivity, while newly planted woodlands are shown to improve connectivity for fauna, flora and fungi. Species interactions featured seed-caching behaviour shifting under predation risk, zebra and wildebeest thermoregulation through a Namibian drought, and herbivorous crabs helping an invasive salt-marsh grass beat a native reed. Invasion and community papers link landscape structure to alien plant spread and show raptor coexistence via breeding-habitat segregation, and Science papers map global threats to freshwater biodiversity and cryptic genetic erosion in birds of a hotspot. On the methods front, Vendi information gain for camera-trap active learning, the camtrapR package, fishmax and an automated drone canopy workflow were the notable tools.
